title: Evaluation of postnatal regional ventilation distribution in the initial care of newborns with congenital lung malformations (ReVent NeoLung)
summary:
Some newborns are born with congenital changes or malformations of the lungs, for example a diaphragmatic hernia, underdeveloped lungs, or cysts in the lungs. Such newborns often have difficulty breathing on their own after birth. Therefore, they frequently require immediate support from a specialized team of pediatricians who take care of their breathing right in the delivery room or after a cesarean section.
Until recently, it was not possible to observe precisely how air is distributed in the different regions of the lungs of these newborns immediately after birth. However, this would be important, as uneven ventilation of the lungs can lead to further complications.
With a new, gentle method—so-called Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT)—this is now possible. This technique works without radiation and can be used directly at the child’s bedside. It measures which areas of the lungs are ventilated and how well, in real time. This allows doctors to better assess which type of respiratory support is most suitable for the child.
For this purpose, the newborn is fitted with a soft belt containing many small electrodes around the chest. A weak electrical current, which is harmless to the child, is passed through it. From these measurements, an image can be created that shows how air is distributed in the different parts of the lungs. This enables doctors to immediately see whether both lungs are ventilated evenly or whether there are differences.
With the help of this method, treatment can be tailored individually. This means that your child receives the respiratory support that best matches their lungs. This can help avoid complications and improve the chances of recovery.
In this study, we aim to investigate how the lungs of newborns with congenital malformations expand and fill with air in the first minutes after birth.
For this purpose, we use the new, gentle measurement method EIT (Electrical Impedance Tomography).

interventions.name: All newborns (preterm infants, term infants >24 weeks’ gestation) with a congenital lung malformation (mandatory: prenatal diagnosis). Description of the study protocol: Immediately after spontaneous delivery or cesarean section (resuscitation of the newborn on a Concord-trolley during pulsating umb

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All newborns (preterm infants and term newborns >24 weeks of gestation) with a congenital lung malformation (mandatory: prenatal diagnosis)
Exclusion criteria:
1) Patients receiving palliative care
2) Lack of parental consent (prior to birth)
3) Contraindication to performing EIT measurement according to approval (e.g., presence of a pacemaker) or inability to perform EIT measurement on the thorax due to wound dressings or indwelling drains.
